topic: A First WTA Title for the Philippines
zh: 菲律賓首座 WTA 巡迴賽冠軍

a.title: A Young Player Wins a Big Title
text: On Monday, August 3, a young tennis player from the Philippines won a big prize. Her name is Alexandra Eala. She won the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, in the United States.
In the final, Eala played against Jessica Pegula from the United States. Eala lost the first set. But then she played better and better, and she won the match.
This win was very special. Eala is the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA Tour title. She is also the first player from Southeast Asia to win a big title like this.
Eala learned tennis at a famous school in Spain. The school was started by the star player Rafael Nadal. She left home when she was very young to follow her dream.
Many people in the Philippines watched the match. They were very proud. Now Eala is a hero in her country.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How rain and lightning stopped a tennis final
A young Filipina player winning a big title
A famous tennis academy in Spain and its students
Jessica Pegula's long career in American tennis

q.q: Who did Eala play against in the final?
opts: Rafael Nadal
Serena Williams
Naomi Osaka
Jessica Pegula
q.why: 原文：“In the final, Eala played against Jessica Pegula from the United States.”

q.q: Why is Eala's win special?
opts: She is the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA title
She is the youngest player ever to win a title in Washington
She won the final without losing a single set to Pegula
She became the number one player in the world that week

q.q: In the text, “proud” means people felt ___.
opts: tired and sleepy
surprised and afraid
honored and happy
sad and lonely

q.q: Eala lost the first set but won the match. This shows she ___.
opts: was lucky because of the rain
played her best only in the first set
did not care about losing
did not stop trying and came back

q.q: You lose the first game of a school competition. What can you learn from Eala?
opts: A bad start doesn't decide the result — keep fighting
If you lose the first game, it is best to stop early
Blame the weather when a game does not go your way
The first game always shows who is going to win

gt.en: On Monday, August 3, a young tennis player from the Philippines won a big prize.
gt.zh: 八月三日星期一，一位來自菲律賓的年輕網球選手贏得了一項大獎。

gt.en: In the final, Eala played against Jessica Pegula from the United States.
gt.zh: 在決賽中，埃亞拉對上了來自美國的佩古拉。

gt.en: Eala is the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA Tour title.
gt.zh: 埃亞拉是第一位贏得 WTA 巡迴賽冠軍的菲律賓選手。

tz: 8 月 3 日星期一，一位來自菲律賓的年輕網球選手贏得了一個大獎。她的名字是亞歷山德拉・埃拉拉。她在美國華盛頓贏得了穆巴達拉華盛頓公開賽。
在決賽中，埃拉拉的對手是來自美國的潔西卡・佩古拉。埃拉拉輸了第一盤，但後來她越打越好，贏得了這場比賽。
這場勝利非常特別。埃拉拉是第一位贏得 WTA 巡迴賽冠軍的菲律賓選手，也是第一位贏得這類大型冠軍的東南亞選手。
埃拉拉在西班牙一所有名的學校學網球，那所學校是由球星拉斐爾・納達爾創辦的。她很小就離開家，去追尋自己的夢想。
菲律賓有很多人看了這場比賽，他們非常驕傲。現在埃拉拉是她國家的英雄。

b.title: Eala Makes History in Washington
text: On Monday 3 August, Alexandra Eala made history in Washington, D.C. The young Filipina defeated the American Jessica Pegula to win the Mubadala DC Open — her first title on the WTA Tour.

The match was not easy. Eala lost the opening set 6–4 and, because of heavy rain and lightning, the final had to be stopped and finished the next day. When play continued, she fought back to take the second set and then swept the third 6–0.

Her victory was historic. Eala became the first player from the Philippines ever to win a WTA Tour singles title, and the first from Southeast Asia to win at this level of the tour. Ranked 28th in the world at the start of the week, she was expected to climb into the top 20 for the first time before the US Open.

Eala developed her game far from home, at the tennis academy in Spain founded by the former world number one Rafael Nadal. She has often spoken about how hard it was to leave her family as a child in order to chase a career in tennis.
Back in the Philippines, fans stayed up late into the night to watch. For a country that had never produced a WTA champion, the win felt like a national moment.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Rain and lightning forced the final into a second day.
Eala became the first Filipina to win a WTA Tour title.
Eala trained for years at Nadal's academy in Spain.
Eala was expected to climb into the world's top 20.

q.q: Why was the final finished the next day?
opts: Rain and lightning stopped play
Eala hurt her arm in the first set
The stadium lost power that night
Pegula asked for a break to rest
q.why: 原文：“Eala lost the opening set 6–4 and, because of heavy rain and lightning, the final had to be stopped and finished the next day.”

q.q: In paragraph 2, “fought back” is closest in meaning to ___.
opts: argued with the umpire
played aggressively from the start
recovered after a poor start
gave up

q.q: What can we infer about tennis in the Philippines before this?
opts: Many Filipinos had already won WTA singles titles
Tennis was not allowed in the Philippines until now
The Philippines has more tennis academies than Spain
No Filipino had won a WTA singles title before
q.why: 線索：“Eala became the first player from the Philippines ever to win a WTA Tour singles title, and the first from Southeast Asia to win at this level of the tour.”

q.q: Where did Eala train as a young player?
opts: At a tennis school near her home in the Philippines
At an academy in Spain founded by Rafael Nadal
At a training centre in Washington, D.C., in the US
At an academy in Spain founded by Jessica Pegula
q.why: 原文：“Eala developed her game far from home, at the tennis academy in Spain founded by the former world number one Rafael Nadal.”

q.q: Someone says Eala's success came 'overnight'. Which evidence from the text best challenges this?
opts: She swept the final set 6–0 after the rain delay ended
The final was stopped and finished on the following day
Fans in the Philippines stayed up late into the night
She left her family as a child to train for years in Spain
q.why: 多年離家訓練說明不是一夕成功。

tr.en: Eala lost the opening set 6–4 and, because of heavy rain and lightning, the final had to be stopped and finished the next day.
tr.zh: 埃亞拉以四比六輸掉第一盤，而且因為大雨和閃電，決賽必須暫停，隔天才打完。

tr.en: Eala developed her game far from home, at the tennis academy in Spain founded by the former world number one Rafael Nadal.
tr.zh: 埃亞拉在遠離家鄉的地方磨練球技，那是前世界球王納達爾在西班牙創辦的網球學院。

tr.en: Back in the Philippines, fans stayed up late into the night to watch.
tr.zh: 在菲律賓，球迷們熬夜到深夜觀看比賽。

tz: 8 月 3 日星期一，亞歷山德拉・埃拉拉在華盛頓特區創造了歷史。這位年輕的菲律賓選手擊敗美國的潔西卡・佩古拉，贏得穆巴達拉華盛頓公開賽——她在 WTA 巡迴賽的第一座冠軍。
這場比賽並不輕鬆。埃拉拉以 4 比 6 輸掉第一盤，而且因為大雨和閃電，決賽不得不暫停，隔天才打完。比賽恢復後，她奮起反擊拿下第二盤，接著以 6 比 0 橫掃第三盤。
她的勝利具有歷史意義。埃拉拉成為第一位贏得 WTA 巡迴賽單打冠軍的菲律賓選手，也是第一位在這個層級奪冠的東南亞選手。她在那一週開始時世界排名第 28，預料會在美國公開賽前首度進入前 20 名。
埃拉拉在遠離家鄉的地方培養球技——在前世界球王拉斐爾・納達爾創辦的西班牙網球學院。她常常提到，小時候為了追求網球生涯而離開家人有多麼辛苦。
在菲律賓，球迷們熬夜到深夜觀看比賽。對一個從未出過 WTA 冠軍的國家來說，這場勝利就像一個全國性的時刻。

c.title: A Scoreline That Told Two Stories
text: When Alexandra Eala completed a 4–6, 6–4, 6–0 victory over Jessica Pegula in Washington on 3 August, the scoreline told two stories at once. The first was a straightforward tale of a final turned around; the second, quieter but more lasting, was that a player from the Philippines had won a WTA Tour title for the very first time.

The match itself did little to make things easy for her. Eala dropped the opening set and then watched the final suspended overnight, halted by the kind of thunderstorm that tests a young player's nerve as much as her tennis. Returning the following day, she did not merely recover; she conceded only four more games, closing out the deciding set without dropping one.

What gives the result its weight is context. No player from Southeast Asia had previously won a title at this level of the women's tour, and Eala arrived ranked outside the world's top twenty — a position her run in Washington was expected to change. For a region long treated as the margins of professional tennis, a first champion carries a significance that a ranking point alone cannot capture.

Her path also complicates the familiar story of overnight success. Eala left the Philippines as a child to train at the Spanish academy established by Rafael Nadal, a decision that meant years away from home in pursuit of a career that, statistically, very few ever reach. The victory in Washington did not invent her talent; it confirmed a bet placed long before anyone outside tennis was watching.

For all the records, the most telling image may have been the least dramatic: an ordinary Monday, half a world away in Manila, where people who had stayed awake through the night found themselves suddenly, and collectively, wide awake.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: Eala won mainly because Pegula tired badly after the long rain delay.
Eala's success came overnight, with one surprising week in Washington.
The win matters beyond the score, as a first for her country and region.
Tennis has now become the most popular sport in the Philippines.

q.q: “She conceded only four more games” means she ___.
opts: won only four more games in the whole match
played only four more games before the rain
admitted she was tired after four more games
lost only four more games to her opponent

q.q: “A bet placed long before anyone outside tennis was watching” refers to ___.
opts: the early decision to leave home and train abroad
the money that fans bet on the result of the final
her surprising win in the first round that week
her world ranking of 28th at the start of the week

q.q: How does the writer treat the idea of “overnight success”?
opts: Fully accepts it, since one week changed everything
Questions it, stressing years of earlier sacrifice
Ignores it and focuses only on the match statistics
Praises it as the most exciting kind of success

q.q: What is the main purpose of the final paragraph?
opts: To give the final score of each set in the match
To describe her plans for the coming US Open
To compare Eala's career with Rafael Nadal's
To end on what the win meant to ordinary fans

q.q: Why might Eala's win matter to a young athlete in Southeast Asia who never met her?
opts: Seeing someone from the region succeed makes the goal feel possible
It guarantees young players a place at Nadal's academy in Spain
It shows that players from the region now win most of the big titles
It means talented young players no longer need to train so hard
q.why: 區域首位冠軍具有榜樣意義。

tz: 8 月 3 日，亞歷山德拉・埃拉拉在華盛頓以 4–6、6–4、6–0 擊敗潔西卡・佩古拉時，這個比分同時說了兩個故事。第一個是一場決賽被逆轉的直接故事；第二個比較安靜，卻更加長久：一位菲律賓選手第一次贏得了 WTA 巡迴賽冠軍。
比賽本身並沒有讓她輕鬆過關。埃拉拉先丟了第一盤，接著眼看決賽被一場雷雨中斷到隔天——這種雷雨考驗年輕選手的心理素質，不亞於考驗她的球技。隔天回到場上，她不只是追了回來；她只再讓出四局，而且在決勝盤一局都沒丟就結束了比賽。
讓這個結果有分量的，是它的背景。在此之前，從來沒有東南亞選手在女子巡迴賽這個層級奪冠過，而埃拉拉參賽時排名在世界前二十名之外——預料她在華盛頓的這段旅程會改變這一點。對一個長期被視為職業網球邊緣的地區來說，第一位冠軍所帶來的意義，是排名積分無法衡量的。
她的成長路徑也讓「一夕成名」這個常見的故事變得複雜。埃拉拉小時候就離開菲律賓，到拉斐爾・納達爾創辦的西班牙學院受訓；這個決定代表她要離家多年，去追求一個從統計上來看極少人能達到的職業生涯。華盛頓的勝利並沒有創造出她的天分；它只是證實了一個早在網球圈外沒有人注意時，就已經下好的賭注。
在所有紀錄之中，最能說明一切的畫面，或許是最不戲劇化的那一個：遠在半個地球之外的馬尼拉，一個普通的星期一，那些熬了一整夜的人，突然間一起清醒了過來。

discuss: Have you ever worked very hard for something over a long time? What was it?
Is it worth leaving your home and family to chase a dream? Why or why not?
Why do people feel proud when someone from their own country succeeds?

a.title: The Sky Is Very Hot
text: In early August 2026, a strong heatwave hit central Europe. Many places were hotter than ever before.
In Austria, the temperature reached 41.2°C. This is the highest temperature in the country's history. The day before, the city of Vienna reached 40°C. Nearby Slovakia was even hotter, at 42.2°C.
In Italy, the heat was also dangerous. The government put all 27 big cities on a red alert. A red alert means the heat can make people sick.
The heat caused many problems. Rivers had very little water. Some countries had to save electricity. In some places, there were fires in the forests.
Scientists say heatwaves like this are happening more often. They say the main reason is climate change — the Earth is slowly getting warmer.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: Why Austria is such a hot country
A dangerous heatwave in Europe
How air conditioners keep us cool
Wildfires that spread across Italy

q.q: What was the highest temperature in Austria's history?
q.why: 42.2 是斯洛伐克，40 是維也納。

q.q: What does a “red alert” mean in Italy?
opts: The heat can make people sick
There is a big fire in the city
The rivers have become too high
Electricity is free for everyone
q.why: 原文：“A red alert means the heat can make people sick.”

q.q: “Climate change” here means the Earth is ___.
opts: having one hot day
getting colder in winter
changing its seasons every year
slowly getting warmer

q.q: Why did some countries have to save electricity?
opts: Power stations had to close for repairs
Rivers flooded the power stations
Everyone used cooling at the same time
People left their lights on all night

q.q: There is a heatwave in your city. Which plan is safest, based on the text?
opts: Drink water and stay out of the midday sun
Play football outside at noon with friends
Visit your grandparents only at midday
Drink less water so the city can save it

gt.en: In early August 2026, a strong heatwave hit central Europe.
gt.zh: 2026 年八月初，一波強烈的熱浪襲擊了中歐。

gt.en: In Austria, the temperature reached 41.2°C. This is the highest temperature in the country's history.
gt.zh: 在奧地利，氣溫達到攝氏 41.2 度。這是該國史上最高的氣溫。

gt.en: The government put all 27 big cities on a red alert.
gt.zh: 政府對全部 27 個大城市發布了紅色警戒。

gt.en: Some countries had to save electricity.
gt.zh: 有些國家必須節約用電。

tz: 2026 年 8 月初，一波強烈的熱浪襲擊了中歐。很多地方比以往任何時候都熱。
在奧地利，氣溫達到攝氏 41.2 度，這是這個國家有史以來最高的溫度。前一天，維也納市達到了 40 度。鄰近的斯洛伐克更熱，達到 42.2 度。
在義大利，高溫也很危險。政府把全國 27 個大城市都列為紅色警戒。紅色警戒的意思是高溫可能讓人生病。
高溫造成許多問題。河川的水變得很少，有些國家必須節約用電，有些地方的森林還發生了火災。
科學家說，像這樣的熱浪越來越常發生。他們說主要原因是氣候變遷——地球正在慢慢變暖。

b.title: Records Fall Across Central Europe
text: Central Europe endured a punishing heatwave in early August 2026, with several countries breaking their all-time temperature records within days of one another. In Austria, the national record rose to 41.2°C, recorded near the Slovak border, a day after Vienna had already hit 40°C.

Neighbouring countries fared no better. Slovakia reported 42.2°C, and in Italy the health ministry placed all 27 of its major cities under a red alert, the highest level of warning, as temperatures pushed towards 40°C in many areas.

The heat did more than make people uncomfortable. Water levels in major rivers such as the Danube fell sharply, affecting shipping and farming. Demand for electricity surged as air conditioners ran non-stop, forcing some governments to ask people to cut back. In several dry regions, wildfires spread.

Health officials warned that heat of this kind is especially dangerous for the elderly, for young children, and for people who work outdoors, and they urged the public to drink water and stay out of the midday sun.

Scientists were careful but clear. No single hot day can be blamed on climate change by itself, they explained, but the growing frequency and intensity of such heatwaves is exactly what a warming climate is expected to produce.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Austria's national temperature record rose to 41.2°C near Slovakia.
Italy put all 27 of its major cities under a red heat alert.
Heat of this kind is especially dangerous for elderly people.
A record-breaking heatwave hit central Europe, causing wide problems.

q.q: Which of these was NOT an effect of the heat?
opts: Low river levels
Heavy snow
Wildfires
High electricity demand

q.q: In paragraph 3, “surged” is closest in meaning to ___.
opts: rose sharply
fell slowly
stayed the same
stopped

q.q: Why is the heat “especially dangerous for the elderly”?
opts: They use far more electricity than younger people
They work outdoors in the sun more than others
Their bodies cope less easily with extreme heat
They tend to live close to rivers such as the Danube
q.why: 線索：“Health officials warned that heat of this kind is especially dangerous for the elderly, for young children, and for people who work outdoors, and they urged the …”

q.q: What do scientists say about climate change and this heatwave?
opts: Climate change caused this exact heatwave all by itself
Climate change has nothing at all to do with heatwaves
Warming makes such heatwaves more frequent and intense
Heatwaves like this will stop once the climate settles
q.why: 科學家說單一事件不能單獨歸因。

q.q: A post says: “It was cold last winter, so climate change isn't real.” Using the scientists' reasoning, what is wrong with this?
opts: One event can't prove or disprove a long-term trend
Nothing — one cold winter proves the climate isn't warming
Scientists say climate change only affects the summers
Winters are not counted as part of the climate at all
q.why: 科學家看長期頻率與強度，不看單一事件。

tr.en: Central Europe endured a punishing heatwave in early August 2026, with several countries breaking their all-time temperature records within days of one another.
tr.zh: 2026 年八月初，中歐經歷了一波嚴酷的熱浪，幾個國家在短短幾天內相繼打破了史上最高溫紀錄。

tr.en: In Austria, the national record rose to 41.2°C, recorded near the Slovak border, a day after Vienna had already hit 40°C.
tr.zh: 在奧地利，全國紀錄升到攝氏 41.2 度，地點在靠近斯洛伐克的邊界，就在維也納已經達到 40 度的隔天。

tr.en: Demand for electricity surged as air conditioners ran non-stop, forcing some governments to ask people to cut back.
tr.zh: 冷氣不停運轉，用電需求暴增，迫使一些政府要求民眾減少用電。

tz: 2026 年 8 月初，中歐遭受一波猛烈的熱浪，好幾個國家在幾天之內接連打破歷史最高溫紀錄。奧地利的全國紀錄升高到攝氏 41.2 度，是在靠近斯洛伐克邊界的地方測得的；前一天，維也納已經達到 40 度。
鄰近國家的情況也沒有比較好。斯洛伐克測得 42.2 度；在義大利，由於許多地區氣溫逼近 40 度，衛生部把全國 27 個主要城市都列入最高等級的紅色警戒。
高溫帶來的不只是不舒服。多瑙河等主要河川的水位急劇下降，影響了航運和農業。冷氣不停運轉，讓用電需求激增，迫使一些政府呼籲民眾節約用電。在幾個乾燥的地區，野火蔓延開來。
衛生官員警告，這樣的高溫對老年人、幼兒和戶外工作者特別危險，並呼籲民眾多喝水、避開正午的太陽。
科學家的說法謹慎但明確。他們解釋，任何單一的炎熱日子，都不能單獨歸咎於氣候變遷；但這類熱浪越來越頻繁、越來越強烈，正是氣候暖化預期會造成的結果。

c.title: When Records Fall in Clusters
text: For a few days in early August, the weather map of central Europe read like a series of broken records. Austria set a new national high of 41.2°C; neighbouring Slovakia went further still, to 42.2°C; and Italy placed every one of its 27 major cities under its most severe heat warning. Individually, each figure was a headline. Together, they described something harder to dismiss: a continent growing accustomed to numbers it once treated as exceptional.

The immediate effects were tangible. Rivers ran low, the Danube among them, disrupting the barges that still move goods across the region and the farms that draw on the water. Electricity demand climbed as cooling systems worked without pause, and more than one government asked citizens to use less power at precisely the moment they most wanted it. Where the land was dry, fire followed.

It is the framing of such events, however, that has shifted most. Scientists have grown practised at a careful two-part message: no individual heatwave can be pinned on climate change in isolation, yet the steady rise in how often and how fiercely these events arrive is precisely the signature a warming atmosphere leaves behind. The distinction matters, because it moves the conversation from weather, which is momentary, to climate, which is a trend.

What lends this heatwave its significance, then, is not the single highest reading but the direction of travel. Records exist to be rare; when they fall in clusters, season after season, the word itself begins to lose its meaning. A temperature that would once have stood for a generation now risks being merely this year's figure — until, before long, it is beaten again.

q.q: What is the central argument of the text?
opts: It matters less for any record than for a worrying long-term trend.
Austria's new national record is the most important fact of all.
This heatwave can be blamed on climate change alone, as shown.
Heatwaves like this are simply a normal part of European summers.

q.q: “Pinned on climate change in isolation” means blamed on climate change ___.
opts: together with many other causes
by scientists working on their own
by itself, from one event alone
in remote places only, not in cities

q.q: Why does the writer stress the move “from weather… to climate”?
opts: To explain how weather forecasts are actually made
To argue that daily weather does not really matter
To define what a red alert means for Italian cities
To show the issue is a long-term pattern, not one day

q.q: The line “Records exist to be rare” is used to make what point?
opts: Records like these are actually easy to break
Records that keep falling stop meaning much
Scientists enjoy breaking temperature records
Temperature records should no longer be kept

q.q: How is the article structured?
opts: History → causes → possible solutions → warning
One country's story → the writer's personal opinion
Effects → records → a weather forecast for next week
Records → effects → scientists' framing → the trend

q.q: Which piece of data would BEST support the writer's argument about a long-term trend?
opts: The exact temperature recorded in Vienna on one day
The number of record heatwaves in each decade since 1950
The number of air conditioners sold in Europe this week
A dramatic photo of the low Danube during the heatwave
q.why: 長期趨勢需要跨年代的資料。

tz: 八月初的那幾天，中歐的天氣圖讀起來就像一連串被打破的紀錄。奧地利創下攝氏 41.2 度的全國新高；鄰近的斯洛伐克更進一步，達到 42.2 度；義大利則把全國 27 個主要城市全部列入最嚴重的高溫警戒。單獨來看，每一個數字都是頭條新聞。合在一起，它們描述的是一件更難被忽視的事：一個大陸正逐漸習慣那些它曾經視為異常的數字。
立即的影響是具體可見的。河川水位下降，多瑙河也是其中之一，干擾了仍在這個地區運送貨物的駁船，也影響了倚賴這些水源的農場。冷氣系統不停運轉，用電需求攀升，不只一個政府在人民最需要電的時候，要求他們少用一點。在土地乾燥的地方，火災接踵而至。
然而，改變最多的，是人們描述這類事件的方式。科學家已經很熟練地傳達一個謹慎的兩段式訊息：任何單一的熱浪都不能單獨歸咎於氣候變遷，但這些事件出現的頻率和強度持續上升，正是暖化的大氣所留下的特徵。這個區別很重要，因為它把討論從短暫的「天氣」，轉向長期趨勢的「氣候」。
因此，讓這波熱浪具有意義的，不是某一個最高讀數，而是事情發展的方向。紀錄的存在本來就應該是罕見的；當它們一季接一季、成群地被打破時，「紀錄」這個詞本身就開始失去意義。一個過去可能維持一整個世代的溫度，現在恐怕只是今年的數字——直到不久之後，它又再次被打破。

a.title: Every Drop Counts
text: In late August, experts from around the world meet in Stockholm, Sweden, for World Water Week. They talk about one big problem: clean water.
Water covers most of our planet. But almost all of it is salty sea water. Only a tiny part is fresh water that we can drink.
Today, about two billion people do not have safe, clean water at home. Many of them must walk a long way to get it.
When there is too little rain, rivers and wells dry up. When there is too much rain, floods can make water dirty and unsafe.
We can all help. Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Fix leaks. Do not waste water.
Water is life. Every drop counts, and saving it is everyone's job.

b.title: The World's Most Precious Resource
text: Each August, thousands of scientists, leaders, and campaigners gather in Stockholm for World Water Week, one of the most important meetings on the planet's freshwater crisis.

The problem is easy to describe but hard to solve. Although water covers most of the Earth, less than three percent of it is fresh, and most of that is locked away in ice. The water we can actually use is a very thin slice of the whole.

According to the United Nations, around two billion people still lack safely managed drinking water, and many more have no proper toilets. Dirty water spreads disease and kills thousands of young children every year.
Climate change is making things worse. Some regions face longer droughts, while others suffer sudden floods. Both extremes can leave people without the clean water they need.

There is, however, real hope. Cities are fixing leaking pipes, farmers are watering crops more carefully, and engineers are finding new ways to clean and reuse water. Small daily habits, multiplied by billions of people, matter too.
The message of World Water Week is clear: fresh water is limited and precious, and protecting it is one of the great tasks of our time.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Less than three percent of the Earth's water is fresh, mostly locked in ice.
About two billion people still lack safely managed drinking water today.
Fresh water is scarce and precious, and the week focuses on protecting it.

q.q: How much of the Earth's water is fresh?
opts: Less than three percent
Less than thirty percent
About three quarters

q.why: 原文：“Although water covers most of the Earth, less than three percent of it is fresh, and most of that is locked away in ice.”

q.q: About how many people lack safely managed drinking water?
opts: Two million
Two billion
Two hundred million
Twenty billion
q.why: 原文：“According to the United Nations, around two billion people still lack safely managed drinking water, and many more have no proper toilets.”

tz: 每年八月，數千名科學家、領袖和倡議人士聚集在斯德哥爾摩參加世界水週，這是討論全球淡水危機最重要的會議之一。
這個問題很容易描述，卻很難解決。雖然水覆蓋了地球的大部分，但其中淡水不到百分之三，而且大部分被封存在冰裡。我們真正能用的水，只是全部當中薄薄的一小片。
根據聯合國的資料，仍有大約二十億人缺乏安全管理的飲用水，還有更多人沒有像樣的廁所。髒水會散播疾病，每年奪走數千名幼兒的生命。
氣候變遷正讓情況更加惡化。有些地區面臨更長的乾旱，另一些地區則遭受突如其來的洪水。這兩種極端都可能讓人們得不到需要的乾淨水源。
不過，真正的希望是存在的。城市正在修理漏水的管線，農民更小心地灌溉作物，工程師也在尋找淨化和重複利用水的新方法。小小的日常習慣，乘上數十億人，也很重要。
世界水週的訊息很清楚：淡水有限而且珍貴，保護它是我們這個時代的重大任務之一。

c.title: A Thin Blue Margin
text: Once a year, in the closing days of August, the world's water community assembles in Stockholm for World Water Week, an event whose calm, technical name belies the scale of what is at stake: the security of the single resource on which all life depends.

The arithmetic is sobering. Water may cover roughly seventy percent of the planet, yet less than three percent is fresh, and the greater part of that is frozen or buried deep underground. Human civilisation, in effect, survives on a thin blue margin — the rivers, lakes, and shallow aquifers that make up a fraction of a fraction of the whole.

That margin is under growing strain. The United Nations estimates that some two billion people lack safely managed drinking water, while unsafe supplies remain among the leading causes of preventable death. Climate change sharpens the crisis at both ends, lengthening droughts in some regions and unleashing destructive floods in others.

None of this, experts insist, is a counsel of despair. Much of the world's water is simply wasted — lost to leaking pipes, thirsty crops, and careless habits — which means much of it can be recovered. Recycling, smarter farming, and the repair of ageing infrastructure could together close a large part of the gap.

What the week ultimately argues is a change of attitude: that water can no longer be treated as infinite and free, but must be valued, measured, and shared. On a crowded and warming planet, how we manage that thin blue margin may prove one of the defining questions of the century.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: World Water Week is a calm, routine meeting that rarely changes much in practice.

tz: 每年一次，在八月的最後幾天，全世界與水有關的人士齊聚斯德哥爾摩參加世界水週。這個活動平靜而專業的名稱，掩蓋了其中的利害有多重大：那唯一一種所有生命都倚賴的資源，它的安全。
算一算就令人警醒。水也許覆蓋了地球約百分之七十的面積，但淡水不到百分之三，而其中大部分是冰凍的，或深埋在地底。實際上，人類文明靠著一道薄薄的藍色邊緣存活——那些河川、湖泊和淺層含水層，只是整體中極小一部分的極小一部分。
這道邊緣正承受越來越大的壓力。聯合國估計，大約有二十億人缺乏安全管理的飲用水，而不安全的水源仍是可預防死亡的主要原因之一。氣候變遷從兩端加劇了這場危機：讓某些地區的乾旱拉長，又在其他地區釋放出具破壞力的洪水。
專家堅持，這一切並不是絕望的勸告。世界上有很多水其實只是被浪費掉了——流失在漏水的管線、耗水的作物和粗心的習慣裡——這表示其中很多是可以挽回的。回收再利用、更聰明的農業，以及修繕老舊的基礎設施，加起來就能補上很大一部分缺口。
這一週最終主張的，是一種態度的改變：水不能再被當成無限而免費的東西，而必須被珍惜、被計量、被分享。在一個擁擠又正在暖化的星球上，我們如何管理那道薄薄的藍色邊緣，可能會成為這個世紀最關鍵的問題之一。

a.title: The King Has Died
text: On Thursday, August 28, King Harald V of Norway died. He was 89 years old. He was the king for 35 years.
The king was sick. He went to a hospital in the city of Oslo. He died there in his sleep, in a quiet and peaceful way.
Now Norway has a new king. His name is King Haakon VIII. He is the son of King Harald, and he is 53 years old. His wife, Mette-Marit, is the new queen.

b.title: A 35-Year Reign Comes to an End
text: Norway is in mourning after the death of King Harald V, who died in the early morning of Thursday 28 August at a hospital in Oslo. He was 89 and had been Norway's king for 35 years.

The king had been admitted to hospital eleven days earlier with a blood condition, and the palace said he passed away peacefully in his sleep. Flags across the country were lowered, and people left flowers outside the royal palace.

He is succeeded by his only son, who now becomes King Haakon VIII at the age of 53. Haakon's wife, Mette-Marit, becomes queen. In his first words as king, Haakon spoke of his father's long service and asked the country to face the future together.

Norway is a constitutional monarchy. This means the king is head of state, but he does not govern: elected politicians make the laws and run the country, while the monarch's role is largely ceremonial and symbolic — opening parliament, meeting foreign leaders, and representing the nation.

Attention has also turned to the next generation. First in line to the throne is Haakon's daughter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, who is 22. If she becomes queen, she would be the first woman to rule Norway in her own right in modern times.

c.title: What Is a Modern Monarchy For?
text: The death of King Harald V, announced by the Norwegian palace on the morning of 28 August, closed a reign of thirty-five years and opened a quieter set of questions about what a modern monarchy is actually for. Harald, who was 89 and had been in hospital for less than a fortnight, died in his sleep; his only son succeeds him as King Haakon VIII.

On paper, little changes. Norway is a constitutional monarchy, which means the incoming king inherits a role defined far more by restraint than by power. He will open parliament without writing its laws, receive foreign leaders without setting foreign policy, and speak for the nation without governing it. The authority that matters continues to sit, as before, with elected politicians answerable to voters.

And yet the symbolic weight of the office is not nothing. In a fractured age, a head of state who stands deliberately above party politics can offer a kind of continuity that elected leaders, by design, cannot. Harald was widely respected less for anything he decided than for what he represented — a steadiness that outlasted governments and controversies alike. His son inherits that expectation far more than any concrete power.

The succession also points forward. First in line is not another prince but Haakon's daughter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, who at 22 would, in time, become the first woman to reign over Norway in her own right in the modern era — a quiet marker of how far the rules of royal succession have shifted within a single lifetime.
For most Norwegians, though, the immediate response was simpler than any of this: the loss of a familiar figure who had, for thirty-five years, simply always been there.
gloss: 憑本身資格（而非因配偶）

q.q: Which best captures the central point of the text?
opts: A long reign has ended, raising questions about a modern monarch's role.
Norway should now end its monarchy and become a republic instead.
The late king held great political power for his thirty-five years.
A long reign has ended, and the new king will now govern Norway directly.

q.q: “A role defined far more by restraint than by power” suggests the king's role is one of ___.
opts: giving orders to the government
fighting for more political power
holding back rather than ruling
doing nothing of any importance

q.q: Why might a head of state “above party politics” be valuable?
opts: He can decide which political party wins elections
He helps parliament pass new laws much faster
He is free to ignore the constitution when needed
He offers continuity that changing governments cannot

q.q: How does the writer view the monarch's lack of real power?
opts: As a serious problem that Norway needs to fix
As balanced — limited in power, yet meaningful

q.q: What is the purpose of the final paragraph?
opts: To list the new king's plans for his first year
To describe the palace ceremonies planned for the new king
To return to ordinary people's simple, human reaction

q.q: Which argument would a supporter of Norway's monarchy most likely use, based on the text?
opts: The king should take control of the government in a crisis

tz: 挪威王宮在 8 月 28 日早上宣布國王哈拉爾五世過世，結束了一段三十五年的統治，也開啟了一組比較安靜的問題：一個現代君主制，究竟是為了什麼而存在？89 歲、住院不到兩週的哈拉爾在睡夢中過世；他唯一的兒子繼位，成為國王哈康八世。
在紙面上，幾乎沒有什麼改變。挪威是君主立憲國家，這表示新國王繼承的角色，與其說由權力界定，不如說由克制界定。他會主持國會開議，卻不寫國會的法律；他會接見外國領袖，卻不制定外交政策；他會代表國家發言，卻不治理國家。真正重要的權力，一如既往，仍掌握在必須對選民負責的民選政治人物手中。
然而，這個職位的象徵分量並非微不足道。在一個分裂的時代，一位刻意超然於黨派政治之上的國家元首，能提供一種民選領袖在制度上就無法提供的延續性。哈拉爾受到廣泛尊敬，與其說是因為他做了什麼決定，不如說是因為他代表了什麼——一種比歷任政府和各種爭議都更長久的穩定。他的兒子繼承的，與其說是任何具體的權力，不如說是這份期待。
這次繼位也指向未來。王位第一順位繼承人不是另一位王子，而是哈康的女兒、22 歲的英格麗・亞歷山德拉公主；將來她會成為近代第一位以自身名義統治挪威的女性——這個安靜的指標說明了，在短短一個人的一生之中，王位繼承的規則已經改變了多少。
不過，對大多數挪威人來說，當下的反應比這一切都簡單：失去了一位熟悉的人物——三十五年來，他就是一直都在那裡。
